title: Glioma Cell Invasion and Proliferation in Ex Vivo Mouse Brain Slices
author: van Asperen, van Bodegraven, et al.
materials: Right before the start of the experiment, perform the following preparations within a biosafety cabinet level 1:3.Prepare the culture plates for collection of the ex vivo organotypic brain slices.a.Prepare 1.5 mL serum-supplemented recovery medium per well for a 6-well plate, by adding 0.375 mL FBS to 1.125 mL recovery medium base per well and transfer to a 6-well plate. The number of wells is dependent on the experimental conditions.b.Place cell culture inserts into the serum-supplemented recovery medium using forceps.c.Place the plate at 37°C to preheat in a humidified 5% CO2 incubator until further use.Note: Optionally, the ex vivo organotypic brain slices can be collected first in cell culture inserts placed in recovery medium without FBS to avoid exposure of the serum-supplemented recovery medium to the open air. In this case, prepare an additional 6-well plate with serum-free recovery medium, by adding 0.375 mL plain DMEM/F-12 medium to 1.125 mL recovery medium base per well.4.Transfer 100 mL artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) to a sterile flask and keep it on ice.5.Transfer 25 mL aCSF to a 50 mL tube for collection of the mouse brain tissue.6.Clean the vibratome and additional equipment.a.Clean the vibratome and working space around it with 70% ethanol.b.Clean the buffer tray and place it in the vibratome.c.Fill the space around the buffer tray with ice.d.Sterilize the vibratome equipment (razor blades, specimen disc, brushes, and spoons) by incubating it in the vibratome buffer tray with a layer of 70% ethanol until further use.Optional: The vibratome can be placed in a laminar flow cabinet to reduce the risk of contamination. This is however not required when the aseptic techniques specified in step 6 are applied.

This section describes the final analysis steps to quantify the number of invaded and non-invaded glioma cells and to quantify the invasion distances (See also Methods video S3). The analysis steps differ depending on the version of Imaris that is used (versions 8.4–9.4 or version 9.5 or higher). Both versions are described below.52.Import the files created and saved in step 51 into the Imaris Software and open the first file in the ‘Surpass’ environment.53.Create a surface (Figure 4B, step 1):a.In Imaris version 9.5 or higher, the first panel in the new surface option is ‘Algorithm Settings’. In this panel select ‘Shortest Distance Calculation’.b.Select the source channel corresponding to the laminin tumor core. Select the smooth function. In our experiments, we chose a ‘Surface Detail’ of 5 μm.c.In the next panel, set the threshold based on ‘Absolute Intensity’. In our experiments, we set the threshold at 2.00.d.In the next panel, additional filters can be applied to the created surface. This step can be skipped.54.Create spots of the individual nuclei in the image (Figure 4B, step 2a):a.In Imaris version 9.5 or higher, the first panel in the new surface option is ‘Algorithm Settings’. In this panel select ‘Shortest Distance Calculation’.b.Select the source panel corresponding to the nuclei of the injected glioma cells. For spot detection in our experiments, we chose an ‘Estimated XY Diameter’ of 11 μm.c.Select ‘Model PSF-elongation along Z-axis’. In our experiments we choose an ‘Estimated Z Diameter’ of 22 μm.d.Select ‘Background subtraction’.e.In the next panel, set the threshold for the creation of a spot based on the quality of the signal. In our experiments we choose a quality threshold of 10.Note: This step will affect the number of spots that are created and therefore the outcome of your measurements. It is important to optimize these settings.f.Finish the creation of the spots by clicking on the green arrows.g.Inspect the spots that are created. Spots that are created based on background signal can be manually deleted in the ‘Edit’ panel.55.Imaris version 9.5 or higher: calculate the distance from the individual spots (nuclei) to the created surface (laminin tumor core, Figure 4B, step 3).a.Click on ‘Statistics ’and go to ‘Detailed’ and select ‘Specific Values’.b.In the dropdown menu, select ‘Shortest Distance to Surfaces Surfaces = x’ in which x corresponds to the name of surface of the laminin tumor core.c.Click on the ‘Save’ Icon to export the list as an excel file.d.Visualize the distribution of nuclei:i.click on the ‘Color’ icon.ii.For ‘Color Type’, select ‘Statistics Coded’.iii.In the dropdown menu select ‘Shortest Distance to Surfaces Surfaces = x’.Note: The values and color coding correspond to the closest distance between the individual spots and the border of the surface, with positive values representing nuclei outside of the surface (invaded into the tissue) and negative values representing nuclei within the surface (within the tumor core).CRITICAL: The function ‘Shortest Distance Calculation’ during the first step of creating a new surface (step 53a) or spots (step 54a) is a new feature in Imaris, only present in version 9.5 or higher. For older versions, skip step 55 and continue with step 56.56.Imaris version 8.4 – 9.4: Perform distance transformation on the created surface (Figure 4B, step 1b).a.Select the created surface and click on ‘Tools’.b.Select the second option: ‘Distance Transformation’. This will start a MATLAB Script embedded within the Imaris Software. Select ‘Outside SurfaceObject’.c.Repeat the ‘Distance Transformation’, this time select ‘Inside SurfaceObject’.Note: After completion of these steps, two new channels will be added. In the first one created in step 56b, the intensity of the signal corresponds to the distance to the outside of the surface. In the second one created in step 56c, the intensity of the signal corresponds to the distance to the surface border within the surface.57.Imaris version 8.4 – 9.4: Calculate the distance from the individual spots (nuclei) to the created surface (laminin tumor core, Figure 4B, step 3).a.Select the created spots, click on ‘Statistics’ and go to ‘Detailed’.b.In the second dropdown menu, select ‘Intensity Center Ch = x Img 1’, in which Ch = x corresponds to the channel that was created during step 56b (Outside SurfaceObject).c.Click on the ‘Save’ Icon to export the data as an excel file.d.Repeat the ‘Intensity Center Ch= x Img 1’ step for the channel created during step 56c (Inside SurfaceObject).e.Click on the ‘Save’ Icon to export the data as an excel file.f.Visualize the distribution of nuclei.i.click on the ‘Color’ icon.ii.For ‘Color Type’, select ‘Statistics Coded’.iii.In the dropdown menu select ‘Intensity Center Ch= x Img 1’ for the channel created during steps 56b or 56c.Note: The displayed values in steps 57b and 57d correspond to the closest distance of individual spots to the border of the laminin tumor core surface. In the file exported in step 57c, values of 0 correspond to nuclei located within the tumor core, whereas values higher than 0 correspond to nuclei outside the tumor core. In the file exported in step 57e, values of 0 correspond to nuclei located outside the tumor core and values higher than 0 to those inside.58.After exporting the data on invasion distance from every brain slice, copy the columns with the invasion distances into a single file for further statistical analysis. The number of invading and non-invading cells can be determined and a histogram can be made to show the distribution of cells within the brain slice (Figure 5).Figure 5Quantification of cell invasion(A) Example quantification of cell invasion. (I) 3D projection of individual nuclei where every nucleus is color coded based on the closest distance to the border of the tumor core. (II) Selection of nuclei that have a value larger than 0 μm, depicted in yellow, representing the invading population of cells. (III) Histogram of invasion distance represents the distribution of cells in the tumor core (AUC = white) and tissue (AUC = yellow) of the 3D representation displayed in (I). The percentage of cells in the tissue or tumor core is printed. Scale bar = 100 μm.(B) Example image and quantification of cell invasion with an H2B-mCherry internal control. Confocal image (I) and 3D projection (II) of mixed H2B-mCherry (magenta) and H2B-mNeonGreen (green) expressing cells. (III) Histogram of invasion distances show overlapping invasion patterns for the H2B-mCherry and H2B-mNeonGreen expressing cells with a similar genetic background. Scale bar = 100 μm.

steps.title: Prepare recovery medium plates
steps.instruction: In a biosafety cabinet, prepare 1.5 mL serum‑supplemented recovery medium per well of a 6‑well plate by adding 0.375 mL fetal bovine serum (FBS) to 1.125 mL recovery‑medium base; place cell‑culture inserts into the medium with forceps and pre‑heat the plate at 37 °C in a humidified 5 % CO₂ incubator. Optionally, prepare a second 6‑well plate with serum‑free recovery medium (0.375 mL plain DMEM/F‑12 + 1.125 mL base) for initial slice collection.

steps.title: Prepare aCSF and ice
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 mL artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF) to a sterile flask and keep on ice; then aliquot 25 mL aCSF into a sterile 50 mL tube for brain collection.

steps.title: Clean and sterilize vibratome
steps.instruction: Wipe the vibratome and surrounding workspace with 70 % ethanol, clean the buffer tray, surround the tray with ice, and sterilize all vibratome accessories (razor blades, specimen disc, brushes, spoons) by incubating them in the buffer tray with a layer of 70 % ethanol until use.

steps.title: Mount brain on specimen disk
steps.instruction: After air‑drying the vibratome, pour the aCSF containing the dissected mouse brain(s) into a sterile Petri dish, remove olfactory bulb and cerebellum with a sterile razor, place the brain rostral‑up on a razor blade, dab away residual aCSF with tissue, apply a drop of Loctite 401 instant adhesive to the specimen disc, and transfer the brain (rostral side up) onto the glue; up to three brains may be mounted on the same disc if aligned identically.

steps.title: Fill buffer tray and carbonate aCSF
steps.instruction: Insert the specimen disc with the glued brain into the vibratome buffer tray, fix it, then fill the tray with cold aCSF until the tissue is fully submerged (≈100 mL). Connect a CO₂‑filled filter tip to the bucket to carbonate the aCSF.

steps.title: Set vibratome parameters and slice
steps.instruction: Turn on the vibratome, set the frequency to 7 Hz and the slicing thickness to 350 µm, then trim off the rostral brain region until the lateral ventricles become visible.

steps.title: Collect brain slices onto inserts
steps.instruction: Using a sterile spoon placed under the blade, gently lift each slice with visible lateral ventricles using a sterile brush, pour off most aCSF, and transfer the slice onto a cell‑culture insert; repeat until four slices are collected per insert.

steps.title: Wash slices and transfer to recovery
steps.instruction: After four slices per insert, remove residual aCSF with a P1000 pipette (filter tip), bring the plate to a laminar‑flow cabinet, wash the slices once with sterile PBS, and if they were collected in serum‑free medium, transfer the inserts to the serum‑supplemented recovery medium plate.

steps.title: Incubate slices overnight
steps.instruction: Place the plate with inserts containing the brain slices in serum‑supplemented recovery medium into a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for at least 24 h recovery.

steps.title: Cut membrane and transfer slices
steps.instruction: Using a scalpel, cut the membrane from each insert around the individual brain slice and transfer the membrane‑attached slice to a 24‑well plate.

steps.title: Permeabilize slices in PBST
steps.instruction: Incubate each slice in 500 µL 2 % PBST (2 % Triton‑X100 in PBS) at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for 4 h.

steps.title: Incubate slices in PBS‑GT overnight
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL PBS‑GT to each slice and incubate at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for a minimum of 12 h (overnight). Handle PBS‑GT (contains thimerosal) in a fume hood.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare 250 µL primary‑antibody mix per sample by adding antibodies to PBS‑GT containing 0.1 % saponin (rabbit anti‑laminin 1:1000, chicken anti‑vimentin 1:1500). Add the mix to each slice and incubate at 37 °C on a horizontal shaker (70 rpm) for 72 h.

steps.title: Wash slices after primary
steps.instruction: Wash each slice six times with PBS‑T (0.5 % Triton‑X100 in PBS) for 1 h per wash (total 6 h) at room temperature (19 °–21 °C).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare 250 µL secondary‑antibody mix per sample by adding antibodies to PBS‑GT with 0.1 % saponin (donkey anti‑rabbit‑Cy3 1:1000, donkey anti‑chicken‑AF647 1:1000). Add the mix to each slice, incubate at 37 °C on a horizontal shaker (70 rpm) for 24 h, and protect from light with aluminum foil.

steps.title: Wash slices after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash each slice six times with PBS‑T at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for 1 h per wash (total 6 h).

steps.title: Clear slices with RapiClear
steps.instruction: Pre‑warm RapiClear 1.47 to 37 °C, add 300 µL to each slice, place on a horizontal shaker at 37 °C and incubate for at least 45 min until the slice becomes transparent; note the solution can be reused a maximum of three times.

steps.title: Mount slices in iSpacer
steps.instruction: Place an iSpacer on a glass microscopy slide, transfer one or more cleared slices (with membrane attached) onto the iSpacer, fill the iSpacer with fresh RapiClear, seal with a coverslip, and seal the coverslip edges with clear nail polish.

steps.title: Store mounted slides
steps.instruction: Store the prepared microscopy slides at 4 °C until imaging. If the membrane detaches, use a spatula to transfer the brain slice to the iSpacer; if still attached, use forceps to place the membrane‑brain assembly membrane‑side down on the slide.

steps.title: Imaris: import files and create surface
steps.instruction: Open the image files in Imaris ‘Surpass’, create a new surface from the laminin channel, select ‘Shortest Distance Calculation’, set surface detail to 5 µm, set absolute‑intensity threshold to 2.00, apply smoothing, and skip optional filters.

steps.title: Imaris: create nuclei spots
steps.instruction: Create spots from the nuclei channel using ‘Shortest Distance Calculation’, set estimated XY diameter to 11 µm, Z diameter to 22 µm, choose ‘Model PSF‑elongation along Z‑axis’, enable background subtraction, set quality threshold to 10, finish creation, then inspect and manually delete false spots.

steps.title: Imaris (v9.5+): calculate distances
steps.instruction: In Imaris 9.5 or higher, go to Statistics → Detailed → Specific Values, select ‘Shortest Distance to Surfaces = [laminin surface]’, click the Save icon to export distances as an Excel file, then visualize by Color → Color Type → Statistics Coded and choose the same distance metric.

steps.title: Imaris (v8.4‑9.4): distance transformation
steps.instruction: Select the created surface, choose Tools → Distance Transformation, run ‘Outside SurfaceObject’, then repeat for ‘Inside SurfaceObject’; this creates two new channels representing outside and inside distances.

steps.title: Imaris (v8.4‑9.4): calculate distances
steps.instruction: Select the spots, go to Statistics → Detailed, choose ‘Intensity Center Ch = x Img 1’ for the outside‑distance channel and save as Excel; repeat for the inside‑distance channel and save. Visualize by Color → Color Type → Statistics Coded, selecting the appropriate channel.

steps.title: Compile invasion data
steps.instruction: After exporting distance data for each brain slice, copy all invasion‑distance columns into a single spreadsheet for statistical analysis; determine invading (distance > 0 µm) versus non‑invading cells and generate histograms.

steps.title: BrdU: thaw slides and dry
steps.instruction: Remove glass microscope slides from –20 °C storage, air‑dry them in an incubation box.

steps.title: BrdU: antigen retrieval
steps.instruction: Cover tissue sections with 2 N HCl and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min; then incubate in Borate Buffer at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for 15 min; wash three times with PBS (pH 7.2) containing 0.25 % Triton‑X100.

steps.title: BrdU: block tissue
steps.instruction: Dab slide edges with tissue paper, outline the tissue area with a hydrophobic pen, then incubate the sections in blocking buffer at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for 90 min.

steps.title: BrdU: primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Dilute rat anti‑BrdU 1:500 in blocking buffer (1:1 with PBS) to make 100–300 µL per slide (volume depends on delimited area), place slides in a humidified chamber (wet paper in incubation box), add the primary mix, and incubate at 4 °C overnight (minimum 12 h).

steps.title: BrdU: wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times for 5–10 min each with PBS on a shaker.

steps.title: BrdU: secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary‑antibody mix (donkey anti‑rat‑AF647 1:1000) plus Hoechst 1:1000 in PBS with 0.25 % Triton‑X100 (100–300 µL per slide), place slides in a humidified chamber, add the mix, and incubate at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) for 1 h protected from light.

steps.title: BrdU: wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times with PBS, keeping slides protected from light.

steps.title: BrdU: mount slides
steps.instruction: Hold each slide vertically on tissue to remove PBS, place three drops of FluorSave (or alternative) on one side, lay a 25 × 60 mm coverslip with one edge on the drops, lower slowly to spread mounting medium, then blot excess with tissue.

steps.title: BrdU: dry and image
steps.instruction: Let the mounted slides dry overnight (minimum 12 h) at room temperature (19 °–21 °C) before imaging with epifluorescence or other microscopy.

steps.title: BrdU: quantify positive nuclei
steps.instruction: Calculate the percentage of BrdU‑positive nuclei using ImageJ’s Analyze > Analyze Particles function or the manual Cell Counter plugin.
